statement: The province should reinstate and raise the consumer carbon tax to cut emissions, even if it increases the cost of fuel.
notes: NDP scrapped the consumer carbon tax in 2025; Greens want a rising carbon price; Conservatives and OneBC oppose any consumer carbon tax. Sharp three-way split that also separates the NDP from its 2024 base.

statement: The province should introduce a wealth tax on the highest earners to fund public services.
notes: NDP and Greens are open to higher taxes on top earners; Conservatives/OneBC oppose; CentreBC cautious. Tests the left flank against the centre-right.

statement: BC should balance its budget even in uncertain economic times, cutting spending to get there.
notes: The ballooning deficit is a top-3 issue for Conservative voters (44%) but near-irrelevant to NDP voters (7%). Conservatives/OneBC centre it; NDP argues invest-first; Greens prioritise climate spend.

statement: The province should override municipal zoning rules to force more density near transit stations.
notes: NDP's signature housing intervention; Conservatives and property-rights voices push back; CentreBC is sympathetic; Greens supportive. Tests provincial power over local planning.

statement: Rent controls should be strengthened and extended to more units.
notes: NDP/Greens favour; Conservatives/OneBC say rent controls suppress new supply; CentreBC cautious.

statement: Supportive and social housing should be expanded even in neighbourhoods that object.
notes: A NIMBY test. NDP/Greens/BCE supportive; Conservatives/OneBC emphasise neighbourhood consultation first.

statement: BC should expand private, for-profit clinics to reduce health-care wait times.
notes: The sharpest health divide. Conservatives/OneBC favour for-profit expansion; NDP, CentreBC and Greens defend public single-payer.

statement: The province should fund more supervised consumption sites and safer-supply programs.
notes: NDP/Greens support harm reduction; Conservatives/OneBC oppose and prefer treatment-first. High-salience values line.

statement: The province should impose minimum nurse-to-patient ratios in hospitals.
notes: NDP/CentreBC support staffing mandates; Conservatives prefer administrative flexibility and warn of cost; Greens support.

statement: BC should approve new liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects to grow the export economy.
notes: Cross-cutting: NDP champions LNG exports; Greens strongly oppose; Conservatives/OneBC pro. Splits the NDP from its environmental base.

statement: The province should stop logging old-growth forests.
notes: Greens/BCE strong yes; NDP mixed and balancing forestry jobs; Conservatives/OneBC prioritise the resource economy.

statement: The province should invest in public transit and rail rather than expanding highways.
notes: Greens/progressives yes; Conservatives/OneBC are highway-focused. Clear spending-direction split.

statement: BC should fully implement the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA).
notes: The defining flashpoint of the 2026 campaign. NDP/CentreBC/Greens affirm; Conservatives call repeal a top priority; OneBC is critical. Even though only ~6-13% rank it a top issue, it is a strong values differentiator.

statement: DRIPA should be amended to make clear that Indigenous nations do not have veto power over resource projects.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC framing; Eby has floated amendments to the NDP's own law; splits the NDP base. Pairs with q37 to map the whole debate.

statement: The province should share resource revenue with First Nations whose territories host the projects.
notes: NDP/Greens/BCE support revenue sharing; Conservatives wary of the precedent; tested by pipeline and LNG benefit agreements.

statement: Public drug use should be illegal and the decriminalization pilot should not be revived.
notes: Eby already ended the pilot; Conservatives/OneBC want the ban permanent; Greens/BCE object on health grounds. Post-hoc but sharply differentiating.

statement: Bail should be made tougher for repeat violent offenders.
notes: Conservatives/OneBC centre street-crime and bail reform; NDP has moved toward it; Greens/BCE worry about Charter rights and jailing the un-convicted.

statement: The province should expand involuntary care for people with severe addiction and mental illness.
notes: NDP has expanded it (and would go further); Conservatives/OneBC want more; Greens/BCE raise civil-liberties concerns. Cuts across left-right.
